acme-dev: Hey team :wave: we've been seeing intermittent 500s and high tail latency on /v1/generate since yesterday evening. Can you tell me which IDs you need to trace this?
ellen: Sorry you're hitting that — we can help. The fastest thing is the request/trace identifiers so we can correlate in our logs. We need any of: `X-Request-Id` from the response headers, the Console Request ID/Trace ID (Console -> Requests -> click row -> Request metadata), or the SDK log lines that show `request_id`/`trace.id`. :mag:
acme-dev: Where do I find those in the Console? I'm in the UI but not seeing a field named "Trace" obvious.
ellen: In Console -> Requests filter by the approximate time, click the entry, then open the "Metadata" panel on the right. You should see a line like `trace_id: t-abc123...` and `request_id: r-xyz789...`. If you're on an older view it might be labelled "Correlation ID" or show under "Response headers" as `x-request-id`.
ellen: If you can't get to the Console or the customer environment, please run one of the following quick repro captures and paste the pieces below: 
1) Curl reproduction (returns response headers):

```
curl -i https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_API_KEY>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Copy the `X-Request-Id` from the response headers (or the full headers blob). Do NOT share your API key.

2) Browser repro: produce a HAR file (Chrome DevTools -> Network -> right click -> Save as HAR) and include the specific request entry. We only need the single request + response headers and timings.

3) SDK verbose logs (JS / Python examples):

JS (node):
```
export DEBUG=redwood-sdk
node app.js
// look for lines containing "request_id" or "x-request-id"
```
Python:
```
import logging
logging.getLogger('redwood').setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
# run your request and paste the lines showing request_id / trace
```

ellen: Things to include in the debug bundle: timestamp range (UTC), region, model, route, SDK version, the request body (or a redacted copy), response headers (full), and any HAR or log snippets. If possible attach the Console Request URL (it contains the request id). Mark the bundle with the root request id so we can link everything. :package:
acme-dev: Got it. Here's the first one we pulled: request_id: r-7f3a2b1c, trace_id: t-ee9c4d2f. Model: redwood-large-v2, region: us-west-2, timeframe: 2025-08-01T18:12:00Z - 2025-08-01T18:14:00Z. Attached a HAR and the curl header output.
ellen: Thanks — got it. Can you also paste the exact response headers you captured (the `-i` curl output) so we can confirm downstream proxies weren't altering things? Also include whether you set any custom headers (Idempotency-Key or X-Correlation-ID).
acme-dev: Pasted the header snippet (no API key):
```
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Date: Fri, 01 Aug 2025 18:12:03 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: r-7f3a2b1c
Trace-Id: t-ee9c4d2f
X-Region: us-west-2
```

ellen: Perfect. Escalating to eng with the full bundle and those IDs. tagging @jason for visibility. :lock:
jason: Looking now — I can see r-7f3a2b1c in our ingestion logs. Initial pass looks like a backend timeout on GPU pool shard 3. Can you confirm whether you were hitting Dedicated or Hosted? Also please include whether you had any concurrent requests (batching) and the `max_tokens` in the payload.
acme-dev: Hosted — no explicit batching on our side, max_tokens 1024, concurrency from our side low (1-2).
jason: OK, thanks. That helps. I'll pull the kernel logs for pool shard 3 for that timespan and follow up. If we need more we'll ask for a short recording of your client-side latency profile (timestamps per step).
ellen: For future reports, the minimal set that helps us right away: `request_id` (or Console request URL), `trace_id`, model, region, SDK version, request body (redacted), and a short note about concurrency. That lets us triage to infra vs model vs network quickly. :white_check_mark:
support-bot: Note: support ticket #SR-2025-119 opened and linked to request r-7f3a2b1c.
acme-dev: Thanks everyone, I'll keep an eye out for updates and can collect more logs if needed. :thumbsup:
